about: What actually isolates an AI build or an imported app's build on a Flagship server, stated as it is (SECURITY-HARDENING-PLAN.md 18.12). `holds` are things the code does and `scripts/build-isolation-profile.test.ts` checks against the source; `doesNotHold` are things it does not do. Nothing here is a claim about a stronger boundary than the one built. Update this file in the same commit as any change to the boundary.

holds.claim: The RUN steps of an image build reach package registries only, through the box's egress gateway on an internal bridge with no DNS and no default route.
The test copy an AI works on is on a bridge that reaches nothing.
Containers on the build, staging and app bridges cannot reach each other (inter-container communication is off).
Staging copies and live apps run under gVisor, read-only, with every capability dropped and no-new-privileges.
The box refuses to start a container whose arguments name the Docker socket.
holds.marker: refusing docker invocation: arg references the docker socket

holds.claim: The AI works on sample data in a separate dev dataspace; the staging files volume is never the live one.
One image build may add only a bounded amount to the box's disk.

doesNotHold.claim: Image builds run on the box's own Docker daemon, which runs as root. They are not rootless and not in a microVM. Compiler and dependency scripts in a build run with whatever the build container and that daemon allow.
RUN steps are not run under gVisor; only the finished staging copy and live apps are.
Base images are pulled by dockerd on the host network. dockerfilePolicy.ts limits which; the pull itself is not behind the registry-only gateway.
Layers are cached by one Docker daemon for all builds on a box. A box belongs to one owner, so there is no cross-tenant cache, but two apps of one owner share it.
A build can still push code out through a registry it is allowed to reach (see AGENTS.md, AI privacy, staging and egress).
